sense: be a burden on someone, take advantage of their kindness

terms.gloss: be a nuisance, be a trouble (to someone)
terms.grammar: phrase: molestus, molesta, molestum, adjective, with esse and the dative
evidence: Plaut. As. 2.4.63: abscēde hinc, molestus nē sīs! (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Clu. 168: nisi molestum est, “if it will not incommode you” (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The polite formula is the neuter: sī nōn molestum est, “if it’s no trouble”. Not impōnere with the dative, which classically means to deceive (see impose).

phrases.latin: ōrāmus, sī forte nōn molestum est, dēmōnstrēs ubi sint tuae tenebrae
phrases.english: please, if it’s no trouble, show us where your hiding-place is

phrases.latin: quōquō tē verteris, praestō est, nūllō locō exclūditur, numquam intempestīva, numquam molesta est
phrases.english: wherever you turn, friendship is there; it is shut out nowhere, never untimely, never a burden
go away, don’t be a nuisance!

phrases.latin: Nōlō tibi molestus esse; aliās veniam.
phrases.english: I don’t want to impose on you; I’ll come another time.
